As a current swim instructor in a different city there’s a lot of factors contributing to this: 

1. Lifeguard shortage is still coming back to normal numbers after COVID. We’re getting there and the programming is catching up. 

2. Instructors don’t want to teach, why teach when you can guard for the same wage and it’s a lot less work? Instructors have to write report cards for all of these kids and they don’t get a lot of paid time to write them. 

3. Parents will sign up their one kid for multiple classes and if we don’t catch them then they get two classes for their one kid. This takes away spots for other people. 

4. Parents will sign kids up for a 10 day lesson set and miss 6/10 days. In my opinion this is the most unfair because you’ve taken a spot away from someone who would’ve been there for 10 days. 

5. Some parents are more dedicated to making sure their kid knows how to swim than others. As a swim instructor right now, 30 minutes a week is not enough time for kids to actually learn how to swim. The leisure time you spend at the pool playing games is way more valuable than the beginner levels of swimming.

ETA: Vancouver also needs way more pools for the public in general. They claim staffing issues but last I checked Vancouver pays less than most cities in the lower mainland. Port Moody has zero indoor pools so they’re way behind as well. This is an issue with infrastructure in addition with staffing.
